description: List the repositories the connected account can reach, most recently updated first, as the options a person picks from. Each option's id is the owner/repo full name, which is what github-list_issues-1 and github-list_pull_requests-1 take. Pass the returned next_cursor back as `cursor` for the next page; a null next_cursor means the last page. This is the browse node behind the github sync picker, so its output is the scope-option shape.

parent_id.description: Ignored. Repositories are a flat list, so there is nothing to open.

query.description: Ignored. /user/repos takes no text filter; see quirks.no_text_filter.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous page. It is a page number. Omit for the first page.

limit.description: Repositories per page, 1 to 100. GitHub serves at most 100.

response_schema.description: Validates the installation response envelope. GET /user/repos uses the repositories array schema below directly.

quirks.why_execute: The sublabel joins two facts into one line and the cursor is arithmetic on a page number. Neither is expressible in the four value-expression operators.
quirks.auth_model: OAuth returns a user token, so the node first reads GET /user/repos. Existing installation tokens receive 403 there. Only that authorization failure selects GET /installation/repositories, which returns an envelope. Invalid credentials and rate limits retain their errors.
quirks.id_is_the_full_name: The option id is owner/repo, not GitHub's numeric id, because every other node in this app addresses a repository that way and a crawler reading sync_scope must be able to use the id it stored without a lookup.
quirks.pagination: GitHub answers with a `Link` header carrying rel="next", which a node cannot read: send_request hands back the parsed body and nothing else. So the cursor is the page number, and a page as long as the one requested is the signal that another page exists. A last page that happens to be exactly full costs one extra empty request.
quirks.no_text_filter: Neither repository endpoint has a text filter. Filtering one page hides matches on other pages, so the node ignores query.
quirks.sort: User repositories use sort=updated. The installation endpoint takes no sort parameter, so existing installation connections keep GitHub's order.
